title: The 10 Best Bolt Cutters
subtitle: Compact, 14-inch and long-handled bolt cutters for wire, chain and bolts, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: Bolt cutters use compound leverage to cut wire, chain, bolts and rod that would defeat snips or a hacksaw. We ranked 10 best-sellers from KNIPEX, RIDGID, Klein Tools, WORKPRO, STEELMAN and value brands on rating, review volume and features (a rating for hard metal, adjustable jaws, cushioned grips and multi-cutter sets).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: GRENPRO 14-Inch Bolt Cutter, Cr-V Steel, for Bolts, Chain, Wire, Rebar and Metal Fence
avoid.flag: Sells padlock cutting with a 4 mm hard-steel limit
avoid.verdict: A 14-inch cutter marketed as ideal for padlocks, though its own listing limits it to 4 mm on hard steel.
reasons: The listing says it's 'ideal for bolts, chains, padlocks', but in the same sentence rates it for hard steel up to only 4 mm. Hardened padlock shackles are usually thicker than that.
WORKPRO's 14-inch cutter, rated higher on hard metal, warns that cutting locks is not recommended.
It lists an '18-20mm maximum jaw opening', which doesn't change what the blades can cut. The WORKPRO 14-inch costs the same and gives honest ratings.

buyers_guide.a: 8- to 14-inch cutters handle wire, small chain and bolts up to about 1/4 inch. 24- to 36-inch cutters give the leverage for 3/8- to 1/2-inch rod and heavy chain.

Capacities are given by material hardness. Soft steel (under HRC 25) cuts easily; hardened steel (HRC 40+) like padlock shackles and high-grade chain needs a bigger cutter. Exceeding the rating chips the jaws.
Small cutters usually can't cut hardened shackles. Use a 24-inch or larger cutter rated for hard metal, or an angle grinder.
Plier-size cutters like the KNIPEX CoBolt use compound leverage to cut bolts and hard wire with one hand. They're great in a tool pouch but won't handle chain.
As blades wear, adjustment bolts or a cam bring them back together so they cut cleanly instead of crushing.
